documents.title: Guidelines for the Use of GenAI in Assessments and Deliverables at SDSU
documents.stance_why: The document requires every syllabus to state how AI "may or may not be used" and has instructors choose a level "ranging from disallowed to unrestricted" (AI-1 to AI-4) per assessment, so it sets no single stance and delegates to instructors with four tiers.
documents.summary: The SDSU Senate requires a generative AI statement in every syllabus from Fall 2025 and gives instructors four use levels (disallowed, restricted, documented, unrestricted) to assign per assessment. Guidelines also cover verification, documentation, privacy, security and instructor disclosure of their own AI use. Only the AI sections of a large Curriculum Guide were coded.

units.why: The Senate rule that "all SDSU syllabi shall include a statement about how generative AI may or may not be used" is a binding duty on instructors to state AI expectations, so P09 (syllabus statement), must, course-start.
units.anchor: all SDSU syllabi shall include a statement about how
units.frag_end: may or may not be used in courses.
units.policy: Effective Fall 2025, all SDSU syllabi shall include a statement about how generative AI may or may not be used in courses.

units.why: "Instructors shall provide clear instructions for the appropriate level of genAI usage permitted in each of their courses and for each of their assessments" leaves the level to the instructor per course and per assessment, so P04 rather than P09, which is about the statement itself.
units.anchor: appropriate level of genAI usage permitted in each of their courses
units.policy: Instructors shall provide clear instructions for the appropriate level of genAI usage permitted in each of their courses and for each of their assessments, ranging from disallowed to unrestricted.

units.why: "Instructors may use recommended template language provided by the Center for Teaching and Learning, or they may develop their own" permits instructors to adopt a template or write their own; closest type is P09 (syllabus statement) since it governs how the statement is produced.
units.anchor: may use recommended template language provided by the Center for Teaching and Learning
units.policy: Instructors may use recommended template language provided by the Center for Teaching and Learning, or they may develop their own as is appropriate to their instructional needs.
units.fit_note: Concerns the source of the syllabus statement (CTL template or own wording), not the duty to include one.

units.why: "The absence of a syllabus statement may be considered a factor" in integrity referrals states a consequence of omitting the statement. It is not a misconduct classification (P36), a penalty (P37) or an evidence standard (P69), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: The absence of a syllabus statement may be considered a factor
units.policy: The absence of a syllabus statement may be considered a factor in cases where a student is referred to the Center for Student Rights and Responsibilities for suspected genAI plagiarism.
units.uncovered_note: A missing instructor syllabus AI statement can be weighed in a student integrity referral.

units.why: The Senate vote to expand plagiarism to include "representing work produced by generative artificial intelligence (AI) as one's own" classifies unauthorized AI-produced work as plagiarism, so P36.
units.anchor: representing work produced by generative artificial

units.why: "Students need to understand the principles guiding GenAI use in assessments and deliverables" opens the university-level guidelines with a statement of purpose and principles, so P56.
units.anchor: Students need to understand the principles guiding GenAI use

units.why: "These guidelines apply to assessments and deliverables within the educational context, not in research with human subjects or otherwise" sets the scope of the guidelines, so P61 (scope), informs.
units.anchor: apply to assessments and deliverables within the educational context

units.why: "To use GenAI effectively, students should have a firm grasp of the subject matter" says fundamentals must precede effective AI use. It is closest to P42 (fundamentals first) although it does not mention novices or courses.
units.anchor: students should have a firm grasp of the subject matter
units.fit_note: Frames subject mastery as a precondition for using AI effectively; no explicit mention of beginners or banning AI.

units.why: "Students must take full responsibility for GenAI-generated materials" makes students answerable for what they submit with AI, so P29 with must; P31 is covered by the next sentence.
units.anchor: Students must take full responsibility for GenAI-generated materials

units.why: "Generative AI can produce incorrect or misleading information, making verification crucial" explains why output must be verified, which is P31 as a fact (informs).
units.anchor: Generative AI can produce incorrect or misleading information

units.why: "Proper documentation is essential for all non-original ideas and sources" requires acknowledgement of sources including GenAI output, so P24.
units.anchor: Proper documentation is essential for all non-original ideas and sources

units.why: "When documentation is required, students must follow standard practices for citing sources" makes citation conventions binding once an instructor requires documentation; P24 is the nearest type, but the duty is conditional.
units.anchor: students must follow standard practices for citing sources
units.fit_note: Conditional on the instructor requiring documentation.

units.why: "The following classification levels determine the permitted use of GenAI" followed by AI-1 to AI-4 names tiers of allowed use, so P05 (named tiers).
units.anchor: classification levels determine the permitted use of GenAI in-course assessments and deliverables
units.policy: The following classification levels determine the permitted use of GenAI in-course assessments and deliverables: AI-1 Disallowed, AI-2 Restricted, AI-3 Documented, AI-4 Unrestricted.

units.why: "Generative AI tools are strictly prohibited in this assessment or deliverable" is a ban for assessments classified AI-1. It is a per-assessment level not a default, so P01 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools are strictly prohibited in this assessment or deliverable
units.fit_note: Applies only to assessments the instructor classifies AI-1, not as a default.

units.why: "Any use of AI will be considered a violation of academic integrity" classifies AI use in an AI-1 assessment as an integrity violation, so P36.
units.anchor: Any use of AI will be considered a violation of academic integrity

units.why: "Students may use AI, but with restrictions and documentation requirements specified by the instructor" defines the AI-2 tier as a permission limited by instructor-set conditions, so P05.
units.anchor: students may use AI, but with restrictions and documentation requirements specified by the instructor

units.why: "Students can use AI in any manner for this assessment or deliverable, but they must provide appropriate documentation" defines AI-3, a broad permission conditioned on documentation, so P05.
units.anchor: Students can use AI in any manner for this assessment or deliverable

units.why: "Generative AI tools can be used without restrictions, and documentation is not required" defines AI-4, free use without disclosure, so P05.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools can be used without restrictions

units.why: "most commercially available AI systems do not comply with HIPAA or FERPA protections" is a privacy fact that informs the later cautions, so P50 informs.
units.anchor: most commercially available AI systems do not comply with HIPAA or FERPA

units.why: "Exercise caution when interacting with GenAI platforms to prevent unintended disclosure of confidential or sensitive information" asks users to protect data, so P50 with should.
units.anchor: Exercise caution when interacting with GenAI platforms to prevent unintended disclosure

units.why: "Always review GenAI-generated content to ensure it does not inadvertently contain sensitive or confidential details" asks users to check output for data leakage; it fits P50 (protect confidential data), not P31 which concerns accuracy.
units.anchor: Always review GenAI-generated content to ensure it does not inadvertently contain sensitive

units.why: "GenAI models can inherit biases in the data they were trained on" names bias as a concern, so P53 informs.
units.anchor: GenAI models can inherit biases in the data they were trained on

units.why: "Validate the accuracy of information sourced from GenAI by cross-referencing it with trusted resources" tells users to verify output, so P31 with should.
units.anchor: Validate the accuracy of information sourced from GenAI

units.why: "Opt for clear and explicit phrasing to improve a GenAI system's understanding of your queries" is prompting advice and fits no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Opt for clear and explicit phrasing to improve a GenAI system
units.uncovered_note: Advice on how to phrase prompts to get better AI responses.

units.why: "GenAI systems may not fully understand sarcasm, irony, or complex contextual cues" states a limitation of the tools, which is not about verifying output specifically, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: GenAI systems may not fully understand sarcasm, irony, or complex contextual cues
units.uncovered_note: States a technical limitation of GenAI systems in understanding sarcasm, irony and context.

units.why: "Utilize your judgment to critically assess the output from GenAI technologies" asks users to evaluate output critically, so P31 with should.
units.anchor: Utilize your judgment to critically assess the output from GenAI technologies

units.why: "GenAI tools are not infallible and should not be the sole basis for significant decisions" limits reliance on AI for consequential decisions; P73 is nearest though the passage does not name decisions about individuals.
units.anchor: should not be the sole basis for significant
units.fit_note: Applies to significant decisions generally, not specifically decisions about people.

units.why: "Be aware that GenAI technologies can be exploited for sophisticated phishing scams or cybersecurity threats" is security awareness, so P75.
units.anchor: GenAI technologies can be exploited for sophisticated phishing scams

units.why: "report any suspicious activity to the IT Security Office" gives a reporting channel for AI-enabled threats; P75 covers reporting suspicious messages.
units.anchor: report any suspicious activity to the IT Security Office

units.why: "Participate in university-offered training sessions to enhance your understanding of GenAI's capabilities, limitations, and associated cybersecurity risks" encourages AI training for the community, so P70.
units.anchor: Participate in university-offered training sessions

units.why: "Stay updated on institutional guidelines and policies concerning GenAI technologies" tells users to keep up with changing guidance; it does not state that the policy will be revisited (P54), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Stay updated on institutional guidelines and policies concerning GenAI
units.uncovered_note: Users are told to keep up with institutional AI guidance as it changes.

units.why: "When assessments or deliverables fall under AI-2 or AI-3 classifications, students must provide documentation regarding their use of generative AI" is a disclosure duty tied to tiers, so P24.
units.anchor: students must provide documentation regarding their use of generative

units.why: "This documentation can take the form of primary source citations or summary statements, as specified by instructors" leaves the form of disclosure to instructors; nearest type P24, with instructor choice noted.
units.anchor: primary source citations or summary statements, as specified by instructors
units.frag_start: This documentation can take the form
units.fit_note: Instructor chooses between citation and summary statement.

units.why: "all factual statements in the work must be attributed to the original sources following standard prescribed citation styles" sets what a primary source citation requires when mandated; P24 is nearest, but it concerns attributing facts to original sources rather than citing the AI.
units.anchor: all factual statements in the work must be attributed to the original sources
units.fit_note: Requires attribution of facts to original sources, not citation of the AI tool.

units.why: "the output generated by GenAI is not subject to expert review, and the source references may not always be accurate" warns that AI references may be wrong, so P31 informs.
units.anchor: the output generated by GenAI is not subject to expert review
units.frag_start: Primary Source Citation: Assignments may necessitate

units.why: The summary statement "should include details such as the name and URL of the AI system, the specific purpose... the prompts that were used" requires tool, prompt and use details, so P25.
units.anchor: include details such as the name and URL of the AI system

units.why: The model text "I hereby acknowledge the use of [insert AI system(s) and link]" is a provided disclosure template, so P24.
units.anchor: I hereby acknowledge the use of [insert AI system(s) and link]
units.fit_note: A fill-in template for the disclosure rather than the duty itself.

units.why: "Instructors of record shall disclose to their students generative use of AI in the creation of instructional materials" requires disclosure of AI-made materials, so P48 (P47 is about grading and feedback).
units.anchor: Instructors of record shall disclose to their students generative use of AI
units.fit_note: Requires disclosure to students of AI use in creating materials; the passage does not mention review.

units.why: "Instructors should provide a rationale when disclosing their own genAI use in order to build trust and model metacognition" asks instructors to explain their AI use; P47 is nearest.
units.anchor: Instructors should provide a rationale when disclosing their own genAI use
units.fit_note: Adds a rationale to the disclosure to build trust and model metacognition.

units.why: "Instructors shall disclose their own use, if any, of generative AI in grading" requires disclosure of grading AI use to students, so P47.
units.anchor: Instructors shall disclose their own use, if any, of generative AI in grading

units.why: The Graduate Council "recommending all programs develop their own policies" leaves graduate AI policy to each program without setting a stance, so P04 (decision per unit), should.
units.anchor: recommending all programs develop their own policies
units.frag_start: Graduate Council provided guidance on AI use
units.fit_note: Delegates to graduate programs rather than to instructors; recorded as guidance only, no policy approved.

notes: Only the AI syllabus requirement (line ~2429), AI guidelines section (~5497) and Senate log entries (~8253, 8267, 8304) of the Curriculum Guide were coded. The standalone dev-host PDF was not fetched.
